answer: Use a decaying action-credit curve: credits decay 20% daily; work replenishes them, but duplicate clusters raise their next registration fee. An opal mark is earned after seven days of nonduplicated work, costing attackers about three credits per identity daily. Each duplicate action emits an echo into a shared cost ledger, raising the next identity’s fee by 0.5 credits. A weekly prism audit samples that ledger and charges 15 credits per confirmed duplicate cluster.
